newsitem.title: CHINA: China, Daimler say project progress slow.
newsitem.headline: China, Daimler say project progress slow.

text.p: Officials of Daimler-Benz AG and a Chinese automotive firm said on Monday they were proceeding with plans for a joint venture but hurdles remained.
An official of Sanxing Motor Corp, based in Zhanjiang in southern Guangdong province, described the project -- announced two years ago -- as in "late stages" of negotiation.
Daimler-Benz was selected in 1995 as the foreign partner in the $1 billion project to produce multi-purpose vehicles, beating out Chrysler Corp of the U.S.
China awarded the domestic portion of the project to Hainan Automotive as well as Sanxing.

Industry officials have said the selection of two Chinese companies has complicated the project. Those two companies are now being merged, and Sanxing officials said that should eliminate some of the obstacles.
The Sanxing official, speaking by telephone, said the main hurdle has been import duties on capital goods.
"We are trying to gain special treatment on property and electricity," said the Sanxing official.
China has withdrawn its duty-free treatment of capital goods for foreign firms though it has given a grace period that has been extended several times.
Many companies are still negotiating with authorities over the tax payments.
A Daimler-Benz official in Beijing said that efforts continued to cooperate with the two Chinese companies on the project.
"The project is not as smooth as we expected. It has been relatively slow," he said.
